newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees progress in tsarist debt talks; $30 billion bonds.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees progress in tsarist debt talks; $30 billion bonds.

text.p: Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said Monday that Russia and France were making progress in their effort to resolve a dispute that has raged for nearly 80 years -- repayment of tsarist-era bonds, now worth several billion dollars.
French savers claim Moscow owes them $30 billion for the bonds, which prior to the Bolshevik revolution seemed like a solid investment.

Moscow, which is poised to issue its first sovereign bond since the 1917 revolution, has previously refused to honour the bonds, bought mostly by French savers in the decades before the communists seized power.
"We are talking about mutual claims. We are checking the volume of debts and a result is possible before the end of November," Livshits told a news conference.
"We want to uphold the principle of reciprocity, but Russia must redeem any obligations it has taken, no matter when," Livshits said.
Russia is keen to avoid any protests by bond-holders that would question its creditworthiness when it launches its first Eurobond later this month.

The problem of the tsarist bonds is also an obstacle to Russia's efforts to join the Paris Club of government creditors, which would allow Moscow to negotiate a return of outstanding Soviet era debts from developing countries.
"Russia is not only the debtor, it also has money owing to it," Livshits said.
